inns.hook: A one-party-per-day private-house ryokan in Higashiyama Onsen, converted in 2022 from the owner's grandfather's architect-built home, funded by the family's horsemeat restaurants and holding nothing back on the room, the minibar or the table.
inns.writeup: A one-party-per-day private-house ryokan in Higashiyama Onsen, converted in 2022 from the owner's grandfather's architect-built home, funded by the family's horsemeat restaurants and holding nothing back on the room, the minibar or the table. the thread author places it among the very best of Tohoku alongside Wabizakura and Kawasemi and says the off-the-charts word of mouth is deserved, after one stay. It combines easily with Atamiso, about an hour away.

inns.name: Yamagata The Takinami
inns.reach: sendai 1h36/1 shinkansen · tokyo 2h30/0 shinkansen · nikko 2h48/1 shinkansen
inns.hook: A 19-room, street-facing ryokan in Akayu Onsen, remade in 2017 under a magazine editor's direction, with a spring-fed bath in every room and counter-seated kaiseki built on obscure Yamagata mountain ingredients, cuisine the thread author ranks top-10, possibly top-5, of every ryokan he has tried.
inns.writeup: A 19-room, street-facing ryokan in Akayu Onsen, remade in 2017 under a magazine editor's direction, with a spring-fed bath in every room and counter-seated kaiseki built on obscure Yamagata mountain ingredients, cuisine the thread author ranks top-10, possibly top-5, of every ryokan he has tried. Book KURA01, the 129 m² first-floor suite with a private garden and volcanic-rock tub, which is the only room he considered worth staying in. It is a lively, social house where you are constantly involved, and he enjoyed that even though he usually prefers solitude.

inns.name: Osteria Sincerità
inns.reach: sendai 1h36/1 shinkansen · tokyo 2h30/0 shinkansen · nikko 2h48/1 shinkansen
inns.hook: Osteria Sincerità is a three-room auberge ryokan on a town-centre lot in Akayu Onsen, built around chef Makoto Harada's Italian-Japanese counter cuisine and an undiluted source-fed cypress bath in every villa, 50 meters from its sister inn Yamagata The Takinami.
inns.writeup: Osteria Sincerità is a three-room auberge ryokan on a town-centre lot in Akayu Onsen, built around chef Makoto Harada's Italian-Japanese counter cuisine and an undiluted source-fed cypress bath in every villa, 50 meters from its sister inn Yamagata The Takinami. There is no view and no garden, and the thread author considers the two-storey rooms more rustic-artistic than pure luxury, but the food is what brings people here, cooked from Yamagata's own ingredients by a chef who held a Michelin star in Niigata. It makes most sense as one night of a two-inn Akayu split.

inns.name: Sanso Tensui
inns.reach: kumamoto 1h42/1 train · fukuoka 1h45/0 train · kagoshima 2h40/1 scenic
inns.hook: A 19-room onsen ryokan in a moss forest outside Hita, built around giant boulders beside a river and waterfall, with bathing the thread author calls second to none at a place he argues is easily among Japan's 20 best.
inns.writeup: A 19-room onsen ryokan in a moss forest outside Hita, built around giant boulders beside a river and waterfall, with bathing the thread author calls second to none at a place he argues is easily among Japan's 20 best. At $420-600 a night it is a real bargain against neighboring Yufuin. The Taisho-era interiors charm some and put off others, and the sulfur smell and waterfall roar are strong enough that sensitive sleepers should take one of the five onsen-free rooms.

inns.name: Tayuta
inns.reach: kumamoto 1h12/0 car · fukuoka 1h54/1 train · kagoshima 2h18/1 train
inns.hook: A 12-villa Amakusa newcomer, opened in September 2024 by a Kumamoto wedding company with no previous ryokan experience, where every suite runs 86–119 m² with a source-fed golden Kinsen onsen bath and island-dotted sea views, and chef Yuuki Nakano's 16-course dinner left the thread author stunned.
inns.writeup: A 12-villa Amakusa newcomer, opened in September 2024 by a Kumamoto wedding company with no previous ryokan experience, where every suite runs 86–119 m² with a source-fed golden Kinsen onsen bath and island-dotted sea views, and chef Yuuki Nakano's 16-course dinner left the thread author stunned. After one stay in the top suite he called it just about perfect, one of a handful of times he has ever been able to say that, and promised it a comfortable place on any future personal top-ten list.

inns.name: Nakanobo Zuien
inns.reach: osaka 1h06/0 bus · nara 1h36/2 train · kyoto 1h45/2 train
inns.hook: A 47-room adults-only inn from 1868 in the heart of Arima Onsen, run as a polished hybrid hotel with carpeted halls, a public cafe and a gift shop, and nothing like an intimate ryokan.
inns.writeup: A 47-room adults-only inn from 1868 in the heart of Arima Onsen, run as a polished hybrid hotel with carpeted halls, a public cafe and a gift shop, and nothing like an intimate ryokan. Its 2023-renovated VIP rooms have their own Kinsen and Ginsen stone baths, a twin-water combination no one else in town offers, and in one of those rooms the thread author calls it possibly the best choice in Arima. Across two visits a decade apart his verdict is warm but measured, a solid luxury pick when you are already in Kansai, though he is not sure he would go out of his way for Arima.

inns.name: Atamiso
inns.reach: sendai 1h/1 shinkansen · tokyo 2h12/1 shinkansen · nikko 2h48/2 shinkansen
inns.hook: An eleven-room ryokan above the Gohyakugawa River near Koriyama that ran effectively private when the thread author stayed in May 2022, taking just two parties at a time, with chef Asano serving and explaining every course himself.
inns.writeup: An eleven-room ryokan above the Gohyakugawa River near Koriyama that ran effectively private when the thread author stayed in May 2022, taking just two parties at a time, with chef Asano serving and explaining every course himself. He calls it one of the preeminent ryokans in Japan and prefers it to its flashier neighbor Suzukane, and only the rooms, which show slight signs of age, count against it. It has been closed since February 2025 for onsen plumbing work and a full renovation, so confirm it has reopened before planning around it.

inns.name: Auberge Suzukane
inns.reach: sendai 1h/1 shinkansen · tokyo 2h12/1 shinkansen · nikko 2h48/2 shinkansen
inns.hook: Suzukane is a corporate-owned ryokan in the center of Bandai Atami run by a former wedding coordinator, with a full suit of knight's armor at the entrance, and the reasons to stay are the food, the warmth of the staff and the big renovated rooms with source-fed in-room onsen.
inns.writeup: Suzukane is a corporate-owned ryokan in the center of Bandai Atami run by a former wedding coordinator, with a full suit of knight's armor at the entrance, and the reasons to stay are the food, the warmth of the staff and the big renovated rooms with source-fed in-room onsen. the thread author loved it and regretted nothing, but was plain that nearby Atamiso is on a slightly higher plane, because Suzukane is in town with only a courtyard for outdoor space and its dining is half-private. It is the one to pick when creativity at the table matters more to you than the view out the window.

inns.name: Bettei Oborozukiyo
inns.reach: see Hiroshima (town) — inn's own leg not sourced
inns.hook: A 19-room inn five minutes' walk from Dogo Onsen Honkan, built in 2015 with a classic look but a fresh, modern feel, and the thread author calls it far and away the top luxury option in the town.
inns.writeup: A 19-room inn five minutes' walk from Dogo Onsen Honkan, built in 2015 with a classic look but a fresh, modern feel, and the thread author calls it far and away the top luxury option in the town. Every room has its own open-air onsen fed by the same spring as the Honkan, and an Iyo beef shabu-shabu hot pot stood out in a delicious kaiseki dinner. He still routes Shikoku itineraries through it years later, as the base for a Matsuyama swing, though he does not treat it as a destination in itself.

inns.name: Kanshuku-en Eshikoto
inns.reach: kanazawa 1h/0 train · kyoto 1h45/1 train · takayama 2h54/1 train
inns.hook: Kanshuku-en Eshikoto is an eight-villa auberge opened in November 2024 by the Kokuryu sake brewery beside its ESHIKOTO complex near Eiheiji, the Soto Zen head temple, and each is a whole-villa rental of about 103 square meters with a semi-open-air onsen bath and Echizen-craft art.
inns.writeup: Kanshuku-en Eshikoto is an eight-villa auberge opened in November 2024 by the Kokuryu sake brewery beside its ESHIKOTO complex near Eiheiji, the Soto Zen head temple, and each is a whole-villa rental of about 103 square meters with a semi-open-air onsen bath and Echizen-craft art. Dinner is at the Michelin one-star Japanese En or the French cadre, with the house Kokuryu sake. Ikyu guests give it 4.71 across 38 stays, with the villas and the bathing their high marks and breakfast the recurring quibble. Nobody in the thread has stayed yet, though the thread author recommends it to anyone visiting Eiheiji.

inns.name: Shogetsu
inns.reach: takayama 1h/0 train · kanazawa 3h/1 train · kyoto 3h06/1 train
inns.hook: A 21-room hilltop ryokan overlooking the Gero Onsen valley, a tall, nondescript building outside but inside all rock gardens, artsy lounges, a spectacular creative-kaiseki kitchen, amazing Gero spring water and valley views from room, lounge and communal bath alike.
inns.writeup: A 21-room hilltop ryokan overlooking the Gero Onsen valley, a tall, nondescript building outside but inside all rock gardens, artsy lounges, a spectacular creative-kaiseki kitchen, amazing Gero spring water and valley views from room, lounge and communal bath alike. the thread author puts it in his personal top ten and far and away first in Gero. The charm is all inside, and the private-onsen rooms sell out early.

inns.name: Hakone Suishoen
inns.reach: hakone in town · tokyo 2h12/1 train · kyoto 3h/1 train
inns.hook: A 23-room Fufu-group ryokan in Hakone that does not use the Fufu name, because it is more traditional in architecture and aesthetics and caters to a slightly more mature crowd, and its dining rooms are set in a Taisho-era Mitsui villa.
inns.writeup: A 23-room Fufu-group ryokan in Hakone that does not use the Fufu name, because it is more traditional in architecture and aesthetics and caters to a slightly more mature crowd, and its dining rooms are set in a Taisho-era Mitsui villa. the thread author returned deliberately, places it right up there with Gora Kadan, Ginyu and Yama no Chaya despite being less celebrated, and treats it as the group's service standard; a later member's stay confirmed the staff as the standout. Book the kaiseki, because the teppanyaki is a pleasant change of pace but it is not the kitchen's best work.

inns.name: Gora Kadan
inns.reach: hakone in town · tokyo 2h12/1 train · kyoto 3h/1 train
inns.hook: A 39-room modern-Japanese ryokan in Gora and one of the thread author's 'Hakone holy trinity', with polished omotenashi, meals served in the room and onsen baths in the first-floor rooms only.
inns.writeup: A 39-room modern-Japanese ryokan in Gora and one of the thread author's 'Hakone holy trinity', with polished omotenashi, meals served in the room and onsen baths in the first-floor rooms only. It 'just missed my top ten' for him in 2022 and is still 'always a solid choice' in 2025, but by then members were asking about the many negative reviews of its condition, and the one dedicated review is a scathing late-2023 member stay (furniture falling apart, room not clean, food just OK) that urges others to avoid it. The service and the architecture seem intact, and the worry is the aging fabric.

inns.name: Yamado
inns.reach: sendai 2h/1 shinkansen · tokyo 4h/1 shinkansen · nikko 4h06/2 train
inns.hook: A 12-room hot-spring retreat in the Iwate mountains with free-flowing source onsen in every room, a private bath suspended over the stream that is worth the trip on its own, and Iwate-proud staff whose hospitality stood out most for the thread author.
inns.writeup: A 12-room hot-spring retreat in the Iwate mountains with free-flowing source onsen in every room, a private bath suspended over the stream that is worth the trip on its own, and Iwate-proud staff whose hospitality stood out most for the thread author. The kitchen does regional fusion led by chicken and pork, which he admires without calling it destination dining. He has stayed once, and calls it well worth the journey for a quiet retreat with authentic hot springs.

inns.name: Bettei Amafuru Oka
inns.reach: see Fukuoka (town) — inn's own leg not sourced
inns.hook: Bettei Amafuru Oka is a 15-room annex on a hill over Kagoshima Bay, the most upscale stay in Ibusuki, taking just four groups a day and grafted onto a half-dormant resort complex, but it has onsen in every room, the sunaburo-and-ceramic-spa circuit, warm Nepali-staffed hospitality and chef Kanemasa Matsumoto's serious French cooking.
inns.writeup: Bettei Amafuru Oka is a 15-room annex on a hill over Kagoshima Bay, the most upscale stay in Ibusuki, taking just four groups a day and grafted onto a half-dormant resort complex, but it has onsen in every room, the sunaburo-and-ceramic-spa circuit, warm Nepali-staffed hospitality and chef Kanemasa Matsumoto's serious French cooking. The bathing culture and the bay views make the stay, and the surrounding complex feels eerie, dated and underused.

inns.name: Onyado Kawasemi
inns.reach: sendai 1h15/1 train · tokyo 2h/1 train · nikko 2h54/2 train
inns.hook: A twelve-room Iizaka Onsen ryokan where every room has an open-air onsen bath and meals served in the room, set around a pond garden, with a kitchen whose Japanese reputation drew the thread author there.
inns.writeup: A twelve-room Iizaka Onsen ryokan where every room has an open-air onsen bath and meals served in the room, set around a pond garden, with a kitchen whose Japanese reputation drew the thread author there. He left an admirer, and the fresh-tatami upkeep surprised him for a place in the boonies. Against that stands the January 2025 stay by jpit2107, who found it luxurious but dated and soulless, very comfortable yet not charming, in a locale not worth the trip from Tokyo on its own. It belongs as one stop on a Tohoku circuit, which is how the thread author places it in his own Tohoku routes.

inns.name: Auberge Yusura
inns.reach: kyoto 2h/1 train · nara 2h/2 train
inns.hook: Yusura is a five-villa auberge near Ise Jingu, opened in 2018, with standalone rooms around a saltwater pond, each with an open-air bath of Sakakibara spring water trucked in from 45 minutes away, and a kaiseki kitchen led by a Kitcho-trained chef.
inns.writeup: Yusura is a five-villa auberge near Ise Jingu, opened in 2018, with standalone rooms around a saltwater pond, each with an open-air bath of Sakakibara spring water trucked in from 45 minutes away, and a kaiseki kitchen led by a Kitcho-trained chef. Service is the standout, a gracious proprietress and a team wonderful with every age, while the kitchen falls short of its pedigree and the Matsusaka beef was the biggest letdown. Five rooms make a full buyout easy, and the thread author calls the whole setup hard to beat, so he has already booked a return visit with the same group.

inns.name: Chalet Ivy Jozankei
inns.reach: sapporo 1h/0 bus
inns.hook: A 2019 all-suite riverside ryokan that the thread author calls Jozankei's premier luxury stay, with Aman-grade design, an involved okami and memorable Hokkaido kaiseki, an easy hop from Sapporo.
inns.writeup: A 2019 all-suite riverside ryokan that the thread author calls Jozankei's premier luxury stay, with Aman-grade design, an involved okami and memorable Hokkaido kaiseki, an easy hop from Sapporo. The one drawback is the bathing, because the source water is tempered with tap water and there is no open-air bath, so Takinoya still wins on onsen while Chalet Ivy wins nearly everything else. Both first-hand stays were happy ones, with nothing said against it.

inns.name: Wabizakura
inns.reach: sendai 2h15/0 shinkansen · tokyo 3h06/0 shinkansen · nikko 4h36/2 shinkansen
inns.hook: A ten-room destination ryokan in the quiet Akita countryside near Kakunodate's samurai district, where the owner drilled 1,000 meters to give a town with no onsen its own hot spring, piped to every room.
inns.writeup: A ten-room destination ryokan in the quiet Akita countryside near Kakunodate's samurai district, where the owner drilled 1,000 meters to give a town with no onsen its own hot spring, piped to every room. the thread author built an entire trip around it and gave it top honors in Tohoku (by a hair), with kaiseki that produced the best fish dish of his life. Reservations are really difficult to get, and repeat guests keep it that way.

inns.name: Kyo Yunohana Resort Suisen
inns.reach: kyoto 45 min/1 train · osaka 1h30/2 train
inns.hook: Suisen is a real, source-fed hot-spring ryokan in the Yunohana Onsen area of Kameoka, 30 minutes from Kyoto by direct train, with an open-air onsen bath on the balcony of every one of its 13 rooms and a kitchen good enough that breakfast matched dinner.
inns.writeup: Suisen is a real, source-fed hot-spring ryokan in the Yunohana Onsen area of Kameoka, 30 minutes from Kyoto by direct train, with an open-air onsen bath on the balcony of every one of its 13 rooms and a kitchen good enough that breakfast matched dinner. the thread author was plain that it is not a destination ryokan like the ones in his top ten. Given its proximity to Kyoto, legit onsen and succulent cuisine, he calls it a great option for people who want to try a ryokan without the time or energy to go farther afield, and a screaming bargain by Kansai standards, unusually cheap for what it delivers.

inns.name: Yoyokaku
inns.reach: fukuoka 1h15/0 train · kumamoto 2h36/1 train · nagasaki 3h/2 train
inns.hook: A 19-room inn in Karatsu, Saga, formed in 1893, with museum-grade Meiji-era architecture, a magnificent old-pine garden, a Karatsu pottery gallery and excellent in-room kaiseki from the local catch, at prices near the very bottom of the high-end range.
inns.writeup: A 19-room inn in Karatsu, Saga, formed in 1893, with museum-grade Meiji-era architecture, a magnificent old-pine garden, a Karatsu pottery gallery and excellent in-room kaiseki from the local catch, at prices near the very bottom of the high-end range. The retired chairman lives on site and will happily host guests for hours in good English. the thread author calls it one of his most authentic ryokan stays ever, and Michaeljinnyc pronounced it sublime. The one drawback is that there is no onsen anywhere on site.

inns.name: Sanso Amanosato
inns.reach: osaka 1h24/1 train · nara 2h15/2 train · kyoto 2h30/2 train
inns.hook: A modern eight-room auberge in deep Wakayama countryside that people book for its French-Japanese dinner.
inns.writeup: A modern eight-room auberge in deep Wakayama countryside that people book for its French-Japanese dinner. the thread author left calling it one of the very best culinary destinations in existence, and stays through 2025 report the kitchen still at that level. Rooms, baths and scenery are comfortable but secondary, since its top-ten spot is earned at the table, so plan it as a one-night gastronomic detour paired with Koyasan.

inns.name: Kumano Bettei Nakanoshima
inns.reach: see Nara (town) — inn's own leg not sourced
inns.hook: Kumano Bettei Nakanoshima is an island ryokan off Nachikatsuura, a five-minute boat ride from shore and the only luxury option near Kumano Nachi Taisha and Nachi Falls, built around a seaside onsen that the thread author calls really nice and, at its best, spectacular and mystical.
inns.writeup: Kumano Bettei Nakanoshima is an island ryokan off Nachikatsuura, a five-minute boat ride from shore and the only luxury option near Kumano Nachi Taisha and Nachi Falls, built around a seaside onsen that the thread author calls really nice and, at its best, spectacular and mystical. Ultra-fresh Katsuura seafood and personable service are real strengths, but only one of the 44 rooms has an in-room onsen and the view is partly marred by oil tanks across the strait. the thread author calls it a good, relaxing base for exploring the area, and says to book Kihinshitsu, the top room, if you can.

inns.name: Fufu Kawaguchiko
inns.reach: tokyo 2h/0 train · hakone 3h45/3 train · kyoto 4h15/1 shinkansen
inns.hook: Fufu Kawaguchiko is the Fufu group's flagship, a modern, youthful hotel-ryokan hybrid that the thread author calls the only choice for luxury travelers in the Fuji Five Lakes, though a slight notch below Fufu Nikko in most aspects.
inns.writeup: Fufu Kawaguchiko is the Fufu group's flagship, a modern, youthful hotel-ryokan hybrid that the thread author calls the only choice for luxury travelers in the Fuji Five Lakes, though a slight notch below Fufu Nikko in most aspects. Everyone likes it and nobody is blown away. His reservations center on the noisy, crowded dinner room and on service that is polished but impersonal for 32 rooms, and the famous view is partially blocked by trees. Book the highest floor you can, ideally one of the two top suites with the open-air onsen bath.

inns.name: Nishimuraya Honkan
inns.reach: kyoto 2h30/0 train · osaka 2h45/0 train · nara 3h18/1 train
inns.hook: The 150-year-old flagship of Kinosaki Onsen and the thread author's annual crab pilgrimage: four stays in, he still names its Matsuba-gani kaiseki the best crab cuisine he has ever had and doubts anywhere ever will compare, served in your room in a traditional house built around a garden.
inns.writeup: The 150-year-old flagship of Kinosaki Onsen and the thread author's annual crab pilgrimage: four stays in, he still names its Matsuba-gani kaiseki the best crab cuisine he has ever had and doubts anywhere ever will compare, served in your room in a traditional house built around a garden. His November 2023 stay found the kitchen below its past peaks, though it stays in his rotation. Book the November–March crab season; bathing is in the communal baths plus Kinosaki's seven town bathhouses, since no room in Kinosaki may have an onsen by town rule.

inns.name: Kinugawa Kanaya Hotel
inns.reach: see Nikkō (town) — inn's own leg not sourced
inns.hook: Kinugawa Kanaya is a 41-room hotel billed as Japan's first Western-style luxury establishment, with shoes-on hotel formality, optional meals and a photogenic garden in Kinugawa Onsen near Nikko.
inns.writeup: Kinugawa Kanaya is a 41-room hotel billed as Japan's first Western-style luxury establishment, with shoes-on hotel formality, optional meals and a photogenic garden in Kinugawa Onsen near Nikko. the thread author put the kaiseki among the top five meals he has had at any top-flight hotel or ryokan in Japan, names the hotel among the few luxury ryokans with a teppanyaki table, and felt the service was perfect. He still gave it four stars rather than five, because the rooms run small for the exorbitant price and he would only maybe return, and that is what keeps the hotel from being an all-time great.

inns.name: Myoken Ishiharaso
inns.reach: kagoshima 54 min/0 train · kumamoto 2h30/1 train · fukuoka 2h45/1 train
inns.hook: A 19-room inn on the Amori River at the edge of Kirishima National Park, with hot springs gushing from the rocks and mallards paddling past the baths, which two “otherworldly” stays made a permanent fixture of the thread author's personal top ten.
inns.writeup: A 19-room inn on the Amori River at the edge of Kirishima National Park, with hot springs gushing from the rocks and mallards paddling past the baths, which two “otherworldly” stays made a permanent fixture of the thread author's personal top ten. Seven springs rise beneath the property and reach the baths untouched by air or tap water, which makes it the most technically obsessive onsen in Japan. The kitchen never repeats a dish, and trilingual attendants like Clement can explain each course and the water itself.

inns.name: Isshin
inns.reach: kagoshima 54 min/0 train · kumamoto 2h30/1 train · fukuoka 2h45/1 train
inns.hook: An eight-villa contemporary onsen ryokan (2008) at the foot of the Kirishima mountains that delivered almost everything the thread author hoped for: standalone villas, private dining rooms and slick source-fed water that he singled out for special mention.
inns.writeup: An eight-villa contemporary onsen ryokan (2008) at the foot of the Kirishima mountains that delivered almost everything the thread author hoped for: standalone villas, private dining rooms and slick source-fed water that he singled out for special mention. The one blemish was the policy of charging 440 yen for each extra bath towel, and a manager who simply said that two per guest is generally sufficient, which was enough that he would almost certainly pick Myoken Ishiharaso or Wasure no Sato Gajoen over a return visit, so it sits just under the region's established inns despite the quality of the stay.

inns.name: Soneka
inns.reach: sapporo 36 min/0 train
inns.hook: A four-villa private retreat opened in 2024 on 77,000m2 of forest and meadow near Kitahiroshima, 30 minutes from New Chitose Airport, where check-in, every chef-cooked meal and two baths of rare amber moor onsen all happen inside your own villa.
inns.writeup: A four-villa private retreat opened in 2024 on 77,000m2 of forest and meadow near Kitahiroshima, 30 minutes from New Chitose Airport, where check-in, every chef-cooked meal and two baths of rare amber moor onsen all happen inside your own villa. At about 339,000 yen a night it is among Japan's priciest, and after one superb stay the thread author calls it his favorite ryokan in Hokkaido, ahead of Shiguchi, because the glorious water, airy villas and dining cooked for you alone are exactly what the rates buy.

inns.name: Fuefukigawa Onsen Zabou
inns.reach: tokyo 1h30/0 train · hakone 3h15/3 train · kyoto 3h45/2 train
inns.hook: A winery-owned Koshu ryokan that gave the thread author a "fairy tale-like" stay, with mesmerizing pond-and-garden grounds and glorious bathing, let down by middling cha-kaiseki, the one flaw he wished away.
inns.writeup: A winery-owned Koshu ryokan that gave the thread author a "fairy tale-like" stay, with mesmerizing pond-and-garden grounds and glorious bathing, let down by middling cha-kaiseki, the one flaw he wished away. Both reviewers agree the magic lives in the Kotogawa and Tsuzumigawa suites, and in a lesser room it is a different inn. At $450–650 a night it is near the bottom of this collection's range, which makes the food an easy flaw to accept.

inns.name: Takefue
inns.reach: kumamoto 1h51/0 car · beppu 2h24/0 bus · fukuoka 2h30/0 car
inns.hook: A vast, lamp-lit bamboo-forest estate near Kurokawa and the thread author's favorite ryokan in Japan across three visits, the rare property that is itself the destination, where a butler of a nakai-san runs everything and every bath is private, though the fully exposed ones can shut in deep-winter snow.
inns.writeup: A vast, lamp-lit bamboo-forest estate near Kurokawa and the thread author's favorite ryokan in Japan across three visits, the rare property that is itself the destination, where a butler of a nakai-san runs everything and every bath is private, though the fully exposed ones can shut in deep-winter snow. One guest proposed here; another left plotting a spring return. At $1,300–$1,800 a night it's priced near the very top of its class, and guests call it worth it.

inns.name: Gosho Gekkoju
inns.reach: kumamoto 1h51/0 car · beppu 2h24/0 bus · fukuoka 2h30/0 car
inns.hook: An eight-room hillside ryokan behind a massive gate in Kurokawa Onsen (renamed Gekkoju Kurokawa), with an onsen bath in every room plus private rental baths, including a man-made cave bath and the exposed hilltop Tenku (go after sundown).
inns.writeup: An eight-room hillside ryokan behind a massive gate in Kurokawa Onsen (renamed Gekkoju Kurokawa), with an onsen bath in every room plus private rental baths, including a man-made cave bath and the exposed hilltop Tenku (go after sundown). With Takefue it defines the top of Kurokawa, and the thread author says the area's luxury drops off steeply after these two; plenty of guests prefer it, and a 2025 visitor who tried both called it 'the overall best for me.' Book a suite higher up the hill for the valley views.

inns.name: Taiza Onsen Sumihei

The onsen in the name is trucked, heated, chlorinated water with a noticeable chlorine smell in every bath, and the thread author says this is not the inn to book if bathing is a priority. The crab is why you go.

inns.name: Hiiragiya

inns.writeup: One of Kyoto's original big three, an 1818 inn facing Tawaraya, and the thread author's third stay was his best yet, because the appeal lies in depth, in layers of craftsmanship and in service that anticipates what you need, and nothing about it shouts for attention. Pick the Honkan for Edo-period atmosphere, the Shinkan for modern light and an elevator.

Only the Open-air Bath Suites and up have spring water in the room, so check the room grade before booking, and book the sushi or teppanyaki counter over the included kaiseki.

inns.name: Minamikan

inns.writeup: A renowned but still underrated 16-room Matsue ryokan that the thread author calls by far the top in all of Shimane, where he loved a full 3-night stay in Mizu no Oto, the 121-square-metre suite with its own excellent onsen bath. All three stays were happy ones, though nobody in the thread has written about the service or the rooms in any detail.

inns.name: Bettei Senjuan

inns.writeup: Established in 1997 as the upscale annex of Ryokan Tanigawa, Senjuan is an artistic showpiece in the shadow of Mt. Tanigawa, with carvings on every beam, a glass-walled corridor onto the Alps and source-fed baths in all 18 rooms. the thread author says it could easily crack his top ten and would not hesitate to return. There is little to do here beyond soaking, eating and the scenery, which is exactly why it shines in deep winter, when the garden turns into a private snow park.

inns.name: ryugon

inns.name: Satoyama Jujo

inns.writeup: A 14-room design ryokan in Niigata snow country built around Keiko Kuwakino's foraged, vegetable-driven cooking at Sanaburi, which the thread author says gets no better anywhere than here and at Enowa. Book The House Izumi, the huge restored farmhouse with its own source-fed bath, because the main-building rooms are bland by comparison. All three stays across two winters were enthusiastic, and there is no dissent.

inns.name: Kinsuikan

inns.writeup: A 39-room Miyajima ryokan that won the thread author back to the island after a disappointing stay at Iwaso, provided you book one of the six renovated special rooms, because the regional kaiseki served there (conger eel, fugu, Hiroshima oysters) is the reason to stay. The kitchen has to carry a large operation, since nobody in the thread has written about the service and the in-room baths are not true onsen, so the inn ends up below what the plates alone would suggest. It is near the bottom of its price class and the thread author's choice for a night on the island.

He would return. Try for Tamayura (Room #505), the only room with an en-suite open-air onsen bath.

inns.name: Kohanyu
inns.reach: see Hiroshima (town) — inn's own leg not sourced

inns.writeup: A four-room adults-only hideaway on Shikoku, built by a retired couple around a lucky spring strike and the owner's world-class vintage audio collection, where the thread author came expecting the river and the food and left most moved by the sound. The cooking is honest local organic fare that he puts below top-10 kaiseki, but the water, the villa acoustics and the personal welcome healed mind and body, and he calls it a refined, adult hideaway. Rakuten's reviewers give it a perfect 5.0, and a member's account elsewhere is just as enthusiastic.

inns.name: Kansuiro
inns.reach: tokyo 3h12/2 train

inns.writeup: A nine-room historic ryokan at Murasugi Onsen outside Niigata, chosen by the thread author over its renowned neighbors for the architecture and radium springs, and he came away calling the charm off the charts, a rare classic property he prefers to his usual wa-modern taste. The cuisine and the top villa deliver without compromise; the mineral-steam bathing culture keeps every bath indoors, and the grilled nodoguro is at its best in fall and winter. He has stayed once so far.

inns.name: Tsukihitei

inns.writeup: Tsukihitei is a five-room 1902 hideaway inside Nara's primeval forest, rescued from datedness by the Miyako Hotel Group's 2023–25 renovations, and it is now the thread author's clear answer to where luxury travelers should sleep in Nara, with first-rate creative kaiseki and a superb rebuilt villa in a setting nothing nearby matches. There is no onsen, and only the three refurbished rooms deliver the full experience.

inns.name: Fufu Nara
inns.reach: nara in town · kyoto 45 min/0 train · osaka 1h/0 train
inns.hook: A sleek modern Fufu resort in Nara with in-room open-air onsen even in the base rooms, and a restaurant set in a historic tea-house garden a shuttled five-minute walk downhill.
inns.writeup: A sleek modern Fufu resort in Nara with in-room open-air onsen even in the base rooms, and a restaurant set in a historic tea-house garden a shuttled five-minute walk downhill. Two member stays in late 2025 loved it outright, and one guest's five-out-of-five verdict put it among the top Fufu hotels, just below Nikko, on the strength of its service. the thread author has never reviewed a stay here and calls it hotel-like and corporate next to Tsukihitei's intimacy, so expect polish and comfort over old-Japan atmosphere.

inns.name: Hotel Ridge
inns.reach: see Hiroshima (town) — inn's own leg not sourced

inns.writeup: An intimate nine-room Otsuka-owned property on a ridge above the Naruto Strait, and the thread author's default refined stop for anyone entering Shikoku from Osaka or Kobe. Service is the strongest part (staff who remembered his wine picks and his room from a cherry-blossom stay years back), backed by a strait panorama he calls breathtaking at sunrise. His first stay left him lukewarm, closing with 'not that type of place'. The 2023 Zeiso villa fixes that gap, and his return ended with 'mission accomplished'.

inns.name: Yunohanaso
inns.reach: see Nikkō (town) — inn's own leg not sourced

inns.writeup: A modern rural-Japanese onsen ryokan perched over the Hokigawa River in Nasushiobara, remote enough that most guests come purely for the springs, the food and the hospitality. inns.name: Fufu Nikko

inns.writeup: Fufu's 24-room Nikko property, opened in 2020 on the old grounds of the Tamozawa imperial villa, gave the town its first true luxury inn, modern and hotel-like where most ryokans are traditional, with an onsen bath in every room and a short walk to Tosho-gu. The flaws are small, a very good kitchen that runs to a Fufu formula and pre-arrival emails that go unanswered, and guest after guest comes away glowing. One couple called it everything a luxury ryokan could and should be, and it has a place on the thread author's own top ten.

inns.name: Shiguchi
inns.reach: sapporo 3h/0 bus

inns.writeup: Shiguchi is Zaborin founder Shouya Grigg's five-villa kominka retreat, the ryokan he says he always wanted to make, with massive restored farmhouses filled with his art and two private source-fed baths in each. Four stays agree it is Niseko's most soulful luxury option. the thread author calls it 'a true gem' and gives the staff's warmth a chapter of its own, and one member put the dinner among the best meals of a two-week Japan trip. At roughly ¥268,000 a night it is one of the most expensive inns even in this company.

inns.name: Zaborin
inns.reach: sapporo 3h/0 bus
inns.hook: Zaborin has been Niseko's established luxury ryokan since 2015, with fantastic hardware, two onsen baths in every room and a loyal following, and the three guests who reviewed it here enjoyed it, one calling it a contender for the thread author's top ten.
inns.writeup: Zaborin has been Niseko's established luxury ryokan since 2015, with fantastic hardware, two onsen baths in every room and a loyal following, and the three guests who reviewed it here enjoyed it, one calling it a contender for the thread author's top ten. But the food and service reports have turned mixed, founder Shouya Grigg now calls neighbouring Shiguchi the ryokan he always wanted to make, and the most recent visitor, who did both back-to-back, would give a single Niseko night to Shiguchi.

inns.name: Ryokan Nishiyama

inns.writeup: A design-forward ryokan in suburban Onomichi, with standalone-house rooms up to 81 square metres, an all-day lounge of complimentary sake, beer and whisky, and a Japanese-French dinner with a wine pairing. The one party to review it, ten people at Christmas 2025, called it a highlight of their trip, with immaculate rooms and extremely high-level service. At $540–650 a night it is toward the affordable end for this quality; the suburban location, with no famous sights nearby, is the drawback, and that one enthusiastic stay is the only account so far.

inns.name: Kuramure

The one FlyerTalk account, an August 2025 stay before a 2026 renewal, calls the dinner, the breakfast and the river-view soaking tub excellent. Ikyu's crowd has been more mixed since then, with the bath their highest mark at 4.22 but food (3.55) and satisfaction (3.78) noticeably cooler and recurring complaints of dark rooms.

inns.name: Iwanoyu

inns.writeup: An 18-room Taisho-era onsen ryokan in the Nagano mountains that is a fixture on the stay-before-you-die lists, and at roughly 40,000 yen a head it is a screaming bargain by top-ryokan standards, which is exactly why the thread author braced for gotchas and found them, all in the lower room categories. Onsen, kitchen, staff and grounds are top notch, but the Sengotei shower and missing bath are teeth-gnashing. Both reviewers left net positive and would return, but only for Senzantei, the four rooms that erase most of the flaws and that you book by phone 11 months ahead or off a long waitlist.

inns.name: Shiki no Yado Michinokuan

inns.writeup: A nine-room ryokan from 1985 near Shiroishi Castle that doesn't scream opulent luxury and doesn't need to, because it is wrapped in forest, serves both meals in the room, cooks delectable local food and is elegantly staffed. the thread author would return without hesitation, but only for one of the three suites with in-room onsen, ideally the top Akebono suite, renovated in 2024, because the six standard rooms share the communal baths and miss the point.

inns.name: Asaba

inns.writeup: A 500-year-old Shuzenji inn that the thread author keeps permanently on his list of top ryokans and calls the pinnacle of Japanese architecture, hospitality and cuisine near Tokyo, arranged around a koi pond, a night-lit bamboo grove and a working Meiji-era Noh stage where Living National Treasures still perform. inns.name: Otogi no Yado Yoneya

inns.writeup: Otogi no Yado Yoneya is a 17-room fairy-tale-themed onsen ryokan deep in rural Fukushima near Sukagawa, its rooms and seasonal 'Otogi Kaiseki' dinner built on a playful (but not gimmicky) storytelling concept, with a six-room Hanare 88 annex added in 2021. The remote setting has nothing famous nearby and the food drew real reservations, but he left calling it a place that stands out.

inns.name: Lamp no Yado

The January 2024 Noto earthquake left only minor damage, but the inn was last reported closed pending structural inspections and power, so check that it has reopened before you plan around it.

inns.name: Shinsen

inns.writeup: A family-run 15-room gourmet inn in central Takachiho, spread across three distinct garden areas, where every meal is served in a rotating series of private dining rooms and the caviar comes from its own locally raised sturgeon. the thread author counts the cooking among the top dining experiences of his life. He has a return booked for late 2026, and a new Beppu annex opening mid-2026 could stretch the staff a little.

inns.name: Wanosato

inns.writeup: An eight-room farmhouse ryokan on an idyllic river in the forest outside Takayama, with cooking that fans and detractors alike call superb; the thread author found the dining far superior to the equally renowned Honjin Hiranoya Kachoan in town. You stay for the setting and the food and should not expect polished upkeep.

The Ikyu crowd gives it 4.70 over 55 reviews, with hospitality (4.84) far ahead of meals and bathing (4.58 each).

Mifuneyama, every one with a private onsen bath, both meals served in your room, and service the thread author ranked above Aman's. The weak point is the kitchen, because for all its regional ingredients dinner did not live up to its tour-de-force reputation on his December 2024 stay. He would happily return, but in bloom season, when the park next door is at its best.

inns.name: Miyakowasure

inns.hook: A ten-room hideaway in remotest Akita with a source-fed open-air onsen in every room, memorable regional cooking and total silence.
inns.writeup: A ten-room hideaway in remotest Akita with a source-fed open-air onsen in every room, memorable regional cooking and total silence. the thread author called it worth a return, both reviewers left happy, and 8 of 10 fellow guests during his stay were repeaters. The interiors have not been touched since the 2005 opening, and the Edwardian furniture jars against the tatami, so the rooms are tired. You stay for the bath and the quiet and put up with the rooms.

inns.name: Migiwatei Ochi Kochi

inns.writeup: A modern 17-room adults-only ryokan on the water's edge in Tomonoura, every room facing the Seto Inland Sea with its own deck onsen bath, where the first night's dinner ranked among the best of the thread author's ryokan-going life. He would place the inn around his top twenty nationally, and Japanese guests near-unanimously agree. Book one of the four Upper Suites, the only category with in-room dining, and know that it stands on a working harbor, so ferry and port sounds come with the view.

inns.name: Yunotani Senkei

inns.writeup: A nine-room cottage ryokan in remote Totsukawa, the highest-end base the thread author found within reach of Kumano Hongu Taisha, with fresh 2017 log cabins and a private open-air onsen he calls pure bliss, run by a loud, energetic and warm-spirited attendant. He says it is not on the same level as Gora Kadan or Wanosato, nor among the top five ryokans he has stayed at. Still, there were no service flaws to speak of, and it has a charm all its own. His stay came at the height of the pandemic in the fall of 2020, and he recommends it as a good luxury option for trekking part of the Kumano Kodo.

inns.name: Tsuchiyu Bettei Satonoyu
inns.reach: sendai 1h/0 train · tokyo 2h15/0 shinkansen · nikko 2h45/1 shinkansen
inns.hook: A seven-room hideaway deep in the Fukushima mountains, built around Shinpeki, a two-level private rotenburo beside a forest stream that the thread author ranks with Takefue's best bath.
inns.writeup: A seven-room hideaway deep in the Fukushima mountains, built around Shinpeki, a two-level private rotenburo beside a forest stream that the thread author ranks with Takefue's best bath. Setting and service run at the level of Tohoku's top inns, and the kitchen is the one relative weakness, finely crafted but below the region's best tables. Book Shinpeki the moment you arrive, because it can only be reserved on the day and the slots go fast.

inns.name: Mt.Resort Unzen Kyushu Hotel
inns.reach: nagasaki 1h15/0 car · kumamoto 2h12/2 ferry · fukuoka 3h/2 bus
inns.hook: A luxury hotel rebuilt from scratch as a modern boutique property, right next to Unzen Jigoku, the steaming sulphur hells, with front-row views of them from most rooms and the lounge, and after a posh 2018 renovation it has a rooftop lounge over the hellscape and the feel of an all-inclusive.
inns.writeup: A luxury hotel rebuilt from scratch as a modern boutique property, right next to Unzen Jigoku, the steaming sulphur hells, with front-row views of them from most rooms and the lounge, and after a posh 2018 renovation it has a rooftop lounge over the hellscape and the feel of an all-inclusive. the thread author's three-night stay in a Hanare room was 'almost perfect', with food he puts up with the best ryokans and hotels in Japan, while Nagasaki Joe on a one-night return found the nine-course dinner good but uneven and the hotel hard to beat for a hot-spring stay in a great sightseeing location.

inns.name: Kagaya Bettei Matsunomidori
inns.reach: see Kanazawa (town) — inn's own leg not sourced
inns.hook: The 31-room luxury annex of the giant Kagaya, which the thread author calls the top ryokan in Wakura Onsen hands down, with museum-grade art in the public areas, gracious staff and fine Noto seafood.
inns.writeup: The 31-room luxury annex of the giant Kagaya, which the thread author calls the top ryokan in Wakura Onsen hands down, with museum-grade art in the public areas, gracious staff and fine Noto seafood. His December 2023 return did not live up to the fond memories of 2016, because the push-button in-room bath is a real flaw at this level, and he now places it a step below some of his other recent top luxury stays. For now the point is moot, because Matsunomidori is being demolished after the 2024 Noto quake and Kagaya is consolidating it into a new building of about 40 rooms due at the end of FY2027.

inns.name: Sankara Hotel & Spa Yakushima
inns.reach: kagoshima 2h30/1 flight · fukuoka 2h45/1 flight · kumamoto 3h18/2 flight
inns.hook: A 29-room auberge resort in the foothills of UNESCO-listed Yakushima, with an ocean-view pool and French-inspired cooking, which the thread author calls as close to an Aman as a Japan property can get, except that the food is better than at most Amans.
inns.writeup: A 29-room auberge resort in the foothills of UNESCO-listed Yakushima, with an ocean-view pool and French-inspired cooking, which the thread author calls as close to an Aman as a Japan property can get, except that the food is better than at most Amans. There is no onsen anywhere on the property and the rates are steep even for a property of this class, but both of his stays were exceptional ("no aspect of our experience caused a blemish"), he thinks the restaurant ought to have a Michelin star, and he would go back for the food alone.

inns.name: Fujiiso
inns.reach: kanazawa 2h/0 train · tokyo 2h18/0 train · takayama 3h06/1 shinkansen
inns.hook: A historic Nagano inn with 240 years of pedigree and many repeat guests, which added two fresh, spacious suites in 2022 with source-fed onsen baths, so you can stay at a famous old ryokan without giving up comfort.
inns.writeup: A historic Nagano inn with 240 years of pedigree and many repeat guests, which added two fresh, spacious suites in 2022 with source-fed onsen baths, so you can stay at a famous old ryokan without giving up comfort. The nakai service is stellar and the kitchen is creative with local produce. the thread author gladly drove the extra half hour for the experience and still recommends it in 2026, but says one night is enough unless you have a car, since off-season Yamada Onsen offers next to nothing.

inns.name: Hanamurasaki
inns.reach: kanazawa 54 min/0 train · kyoto 1h36/1 train · takayama 2h48/1 train
inns.hook: A large, modern luxury ryokan above the Kakusenkei gorge, and the food (spectacular winter snow crab above all) is the main reason anyone comes; source-fed bathing reaches only its top suites.
inns.writeup: A large, modern luxury ryokan above the Kakusenkei gorge, and the food (spectacular winter snow crab above all) is the main reason anyone comes; source-fed bathing reaches only its top suites. the thread author's reservations (restaurant-only dining, a view-less private bath, baffling ordering) kept it at 'merely one of the top choices in Hokuriku' for him in 2018; the 2024 renovation and simplified set menu have since answered some of that, and a 2025 guest called it the perfect choice for a food-first stay.

inns.name: Kayotei
inns.reach: kanazawa 54 min/0 train · kyoto 1h36/1 train · takayama 2h48/1 train
inns.hook: A ten-room, family-run classic that delivers the traditional ryokan feeling in spades (riverside seclusion, antiques in the hallways, dinner in a private room), and the thread author still calls it a tad overrated, because across repeat stays it never excelled at any one thing: the food is good but not great, the rooms decent and minimalist, and the service not quite as personalized as you would expect from so small a family-run house.
inns.writeup: A ten-room, family-run classic that delivers the traditional ryokan feeling in spades (riverside seclusion, antiques in the hallways, dinner in a private room), and the thread author still calls it a tad overrated, because across repeat stays it never excelled at any one thing: the food is good but not great, the rooms decent and minimalist, and the service not quite as personalized as you would expect from so small a family-run house. It is a lovely, authentic first ryokan for a traditionalist, but it is not a destination in itself, and he says the same of the whole Kaga area.

inns.name: Beniya Mukayu
inns.reach: kanazawa 36 min/0 train · kyoto 2h/1 train · takayama 2h36/1 train
inns.hook: A stylish Japanese-modern ryokan in Yamashiro Onsen that does almost everything right (a top suite the thread author called perfect, in-room onsen, gorgeous grounds, an excellent crab-season kitchen), and then serves dinner in one shared, echoing dining hall with no private or in-room option.
inns.writeup: A stylish Japanese-modern ryokan in Yamashiro Onsen that does almost everything right (a top suite the thread author called perfect, in-room onsen, gorgeous grounds, an excellent crab-season kitchen), and then serves dinner in one shared, echoing dining hall with no private or in-room option. That single flaw is why he gave it a rare reserved verdict, is "not in love" with it, and would try neighbors before returning, even as crowds and ryokan first-timers adore it. Book a top suite and the earliest dinner seating.

inns.name: Yado Shiontei
inns.reach: see Hiroshima (town) — inn's own leg not sourced
inns.hook: A 10-room crab ryokan that opened in 2021 in Kaike Onsen, with modern hardware built to a very high quality, all-suite rooms on the area's saltwater spring and service Fc912 called pretty perfect, but the crab itself ranked below Nishimuraya and Bouyourou for the two parties who tried it, at roughly double Nishimuraya's per-person rate.
inns.writeup: A 10-room crab ryokan that opened in 2021 in Kaike Onsen, with modern hardware built to a very high quality, all-suite rooms on the area's saltwater spring and service Fc912 called pretty perfect, but the crab itself ranked below Nishimuraya and Bouyourou for the two parties who tried it, at roughly double Nishimuraya's per-person rate. The building and the rare water justify a stay; if the Matsuba-gani course is what matters most, both reviewers point you elsewhere.

inns.name: NEOLD Private House
inns.reach: nara in town · kyoto 45 min/0 train · osaka 1h/0 train
inns.hook: A one-party kominka retreat in sacred Yoshino that offers the widest range of traditional Japanese activities the thread author has seen anywhere: Noh, geisha, tea ceremony, calligraphy, river fishing, and a full Shogun experience with an Osaka action cast.
inns.writeup: A one-party kominka retreat in sacred Yoshino that offers the widest range of traditional Japanese activities the thread author has seen anywhere: Noh, geisha, tea ceremony, calligraphy, river fishing, and a full Shogun experience with an Osaka action cast. He calls it one-of-a-kind and a must-visit for private cultural immersion, and he is certain to return. That verdict puts it higher than the lodging alone would, since the beddings trail the top houses and the baths are heated water with no onsen.

inns.name: Shoraiso
inns.reach: kanazawa 2h12/1 train · tokyo 2h36/1 train · takayama 3h24/2 shinkansen
inns.hook: A five-room inn re-opened in 2024 a five-minute drive from the Jigokudani snow-monkey park, with large in-room onsen baths (bigger than Takinami's, by the thread author's research) and dinner served in-room or in private rooms.
inns.writeup: A five-room inn re-opened in 2024 a five-minute drive from the Jigokudani snow-monkey park, with large in-room onsen baths (bigger than Takinami's, by the thread author's research) and dinner served in-room or in private rooms. Ikyu guests put it at 4.86 over 90 reviews and mostly rave, though a minority found the kaiseki unmemorable and the main bath a walk to the older sister property. It looks promising, and the crowd largely loves it.

inns.name: Sanso Murata
inns.reach: beppu 1h/0 bus · fukuoka 2h10/0 train · kumamoto 2h24/1 train
inns.hook: A 12-room Yufuin inn whose plain grounds hide the best service the thread author has encountered anywhere in Japan (four staff rushing out with umbrellas in a storm, a butler dedicated exclusively to your room for every meal) and a spectacular kaiseki kitchen that shows off Kyushu's meat, fish and produce.
inns.writeup: A 12-room Yufuin inn whose plain grounds hide the best service the thread author has encountered anywhere in Japan (four staff rushing out with umbrellas in a storm, a butler dedicated exclusively to your room for every meal) and a spectacular kaiseki kitchen that shows off Kyushu's meat, fish and produce. After two nights of "pure bliss" he agrees without hesitation with Japan's own word of mouth that this is a top-10 property in the country. The magic is all indoors, and each of the 12 rooms has its own character.

inns.name: Enowa Yufuin
inns.reach: beppu 1h/0 bus · fukuoka 2h10/0 train · kumamoto 2h24/1 train
inns.hook: An ultra-modern 18-room newcomer (June 2023) on a hilltop farm above the Yufuin valley, built around Tashi Gyamtso's vegetable-driven cooking, which the thread author found eclipsed even SingleThread and called reason alone to stay.
inns.writeup: An ultra-modern 18-room newcomer (June 2023) on a hilltop farm above the Yufuin valley, built around Tashi Gyamtso's vegetable-driven cooking, which the thread author found eclipsed even SingleThread and called reason alone to stay. Rooms are huge with kakenagashi onsen in every one; service was still green in late 2024, though later guests report no such stumbles. Book a Villa or Pavilion, because most other rooms have no view or pool, and plan the stay around dinner.

inns.name: Kamenoi Besso
inns.reach: beppu 1h/0 bus · fukuoka 2h10/0 train · kumamoto 2h24/1 train
inns.hook: A 1921 lakeside estate on Lake Kinrin at the foot of Mt. Yufu, with seventeen rooms all built differently, garden-source kakenagashi in every tub and public rooms (a teahouse, a bar, a gramophone lounge) that guests keep writing about.
inns.writeup: A 1921 lakeside estate on Lake Kinrin at the foot of Mt. Yufu, with seventeen rooms all built differently, garden-source kakenagashi in every tub and public rooms (a teahouse, a bar, a gramophone lounge) that guests keep writing about. It holds Two Michelin Keys in 2025, one of only twenty properties in Japan to do so. the thread author calls it 'the original luxury Yufuin inn' and has a return booked for November 2026. Ikyu's crowd (4.87 across 122 reviews) ranks it near the top of Kyushu, and dinner is the one softer note. Nobody in the thread has written a full review yet.

inns.name: Arcana Izu
inns.reach: tokyo 2h12/1 train · hakone 2h24/2 train · kyoto 3h03/1 train
inns.hook: A 16-suite auberge above the Kano River whose French-Japanese kitchen the thread author ranks with the best restaurants of Tokyo and Paris.
inns.writeup: A 16-suite auberge above the Kano River whose French-Japanese kitchen the thread author ranks with the best restaurants of Tokyo and Paris. Everything else trails the food, since the rooms are comfortable but dated, and an October 2025 guest found the room tired and the service transactional. With Asaba fifteen minutes away, it works best as a one-night fusion interlude between traditional ryokans, and the thread author is not sure it is worth going out of your way for on its own.

hotels.name: Palace Hotel Tokyo
hotels.area: Marunouchi, on the Imperial Palace moat
hotels.why: Tokyo's best Japanese-run luxury hotel, and the one FlyerTalk's regulars pick first: grand but not stiff, with the most polished service in the city. Rooms are large by Tokyo standards and most have a balcony over the Imperial Palace moat, a view no other hotel has. Six restaurants and bars, a real spa and pool, and the palace gardens across the water for a morning walk. Marunouchi puts Tokyo Station minutes away.

hotels.name: The Okura Tokyo
hotels.why: Two buildings on the Okura hill, rebuilt in 2019 around the famous 1962 lobby and the Orchid Bar. The Prestige Tower is the main hotel. The Heritage Wing is the one to know: a low, quiet building with its own entrance and check-in, 140 rooms from 60 square metres, each with a deep Japanese soaking bath and a steam sauna, and the most attentive service in the house. The nearest stations are a 10 to 15 minute walk; taxis are plentiful and cheap in Tokyo.

hotels.name: Hoshinoya Tokyo
hotels.why: A ryokan built as a tower in Otemachi, where shoes come off at the door and stay off. Each floor has a shared lounge with tea and snacks, and the roof has an open-air bath fed by a hot spring drilled under the city. Rooms run 40 to 80 square metres, larger than most hotels on this list. Offices hem it in, so there is no view. FlyerTalk's ryokan regulars would send people to the countryside instead: a tower ryokan is not the countryside.

hotels.name: K5
hotels.why: A design hotel in a converted pre-war bank in Kabutocho, Tokyo's old stock-exchange quarter, and the building is the reason to book it. Twenty rooms, with indigo-dyed fabric hung where walls would be. The basement cocktail bar, a Brooklyn Brewery taproom and a coffee counter are all in the house. The quarter is offices and shutters on a Sunday; Ginza is a 15-minute walk.

hotels.name: SOIL Nihonbashi
hotels.why: A small design-led hotel over its own cafe and sake bar in Bakurocho, the old textile-wholesale district. Raw plaster, timber and steel inside, and guests use the ground floor as a living room. Rooms are compact, which is the trade for the address. Nihonbashi and Akihabara are each a short walk, and the Asakusa line runs from the corner.

hotels.name: Park Hyatt Tokyo
hotels.group: If you hold Hyatt or Chase points
hotels.area: Nishi-Shinjuku, top of the Shinjuku Park Tower
hotels.why: Tokyo's most famous luxury hotel, and for thirty years the one the others are measured against: hushed, spacious and high above the city on the top fourteen floors of a Shinjuku tower, the hotel Lost in Translation made known around the world. The 52nd-floor New York Bar, the glass-roofed pool and the calm are what people come back for; a full 2025 renovation refreshed it without changing it. Nishi-Shinjuku is out of the way; taxis are plentiful and cheap, so most evenings start with one.

hotels.name: Hotel Toranomon Hills
hotels.group: If you hold Hyatt or Chase points
hotels.why: An upmarket hotel on floors 11 to 14 of the Toranomon Hills Station Tower, and the one FlyerTalk regulars book over the Andaz next door. Its 204 rooms are pale wood and stone, quieter than the tower around them. Le Pristine, a Belgian dining room, is downstairs, and the Hibiya line runs from the basement. Toranomon Yokocho, an alley of 26 small restaurants, is in the next tower. Ginza is two stops when the district empties after work.

hotels.name: Hyatt Centric Ginza Tokyo
hotels.group: If you hold Hyatt or Chase points
hotels.why: A competent mid-range chain hotel whose case is its address and its points. It stands on Namiki-dori, the tree-lined Ginza street where the small bars and counters are, so dinner is a walk from the door rather than a taxi, and the Ginza subway lines are two minutes away. Rooms are plain and about 25 square metres; nothing else about the place is special. Take it when points cover the nights, or when the budget is mid-range and Ginza is the ask.

hotels.name: Hotel The Mitsui Kyoto
hotels.why: The Mitsui family's 300-year-old gate is the entrance, and the hotel behind it faces Nijo Castle: the grandest address in the city. Rooms sit around a pond garden, and the spa runs on hot-spring water drilled a kilometre down, the only one under a central Kyoto hotel. The hardware, the concierge and the Japanese breakfast draw praise; a few FlyerTalk regulars found the service formal rather than warm.

hotels.name: Ace Hotel Kyoto
hotels.why: A design hotel built into a 1920s telephone exchange at Karasuma-Oike, in the middle of the central grid. The lobby works as a public room, cafe at one end and bar at the other, with two restaurants opening onto the street. It is the liveliest hotel in this Kyoto list and the easiest to come back to at midnight. Ask for a room away from the lobby side if you sleep early.

hotels.name: Genji Kyoto
hotels.why: A small design hotel on the Kamo river at Gojo, and the water is the point: nineteen rooms, nine of them with balconies over it. Cherry floors, hiba cypress tubs and furniture made by hand in the city. The riverbank path starts at the door and runs the length of Kyoto. It sells out early, so book before the rest of the trip is fixed.

hotels.name: Kyokoyado Muromachi Yutone
hotels.why: A seven-room townhouse inn in Muromachi, the old silk-trading district, with its own Kyoto-cuisine kitchen, which is rare inside the central grid. Dinner and breakfast are served in the house. Nishiki market is a few minutes away. Availability seldom shows on the usual sites, so ask the inn direct or book through Ikyu, the Japanese booking site.

hotels.name: Higashiyama Shikikaboku
hotels.why: An all-suite hotel on a Higashiyama canal, where each of the eight suites has its own front door and kitchen. Two open-air baths and a terrace on the top floor face the red gate of Heian Shrine. There is no restaurant, so the concierge books tables nearby, and dinner has to be planned rather than walked into. It suits people who want privacy more than hotel service.

hotels.name: Sowaka
hotels.area: Gion, in the Yasaka side streets
hotels.why: A hundred-year-old Gion house that was a high-end ryotei restaurant before it was a hotel, in the side streets below Yasaka Shrine. Eleven rooms are in the old house and twelve in a newer annex; the old house is the one to book. A FlyerTalk regular prefers it to the big Kyoto luxury hotels, which he finds contrived, and remembers hinoki cypress and sake in the fridge.

hotels.name: nol kyoto sanjo
hotels.why: A century-old machiya on Sanjo that was the Kyoto shop of the Kinshi Masamune sake brewery, and the old sign is still over the door. All 48 rooms have a hinoki cypress bath, and the lounge in the old building pours the brewery's sake. It is built round a courtyard garden. Nishiki market and the Karasuma subway are each a few minutes on foot.

hotels.name: Conrad Osaka
hotels.area: Nakanoshima, floors 33–40 of Festival Tower West
hotels.why: A luxury hotel on the top floors of a Nakanoshima tower, and the one FlyerTalk picks among Osaka's big names: a member chose it over the Waldorf and called it stunning. Reception, the bar and both restaurants are 200 metres up, with a river on either side. Rooms start at 50 square metres, large for Osaka. He rated the breakfast above the Conrad Tokyo's and the buffet dinner poor, so eat dinner out.

hotels.name: Four Seasons Hotel Osaka
hotels.area: Dōjima, floors 1–2 and 28–37 of a tower
hotels.why: The 28th floor, Gensui, is what sets it apart: 21 tatami rooms with futons and a tea lounge of their own, inside a Dojima tower that opened in 2024. The thread's most-travelled luxury regular calls it the city's only ultra-luxury house and nobody has argued, though he judged the Gensui premium not worth paying and the pool thin for a flagship. Soaking baths with city views in the spa; Umeda station is ten minutes on foot.

hotels.name: Waldorf Astoria Osaka
hotels.why: Japan's first Waldorf Astoria, on the top floors of the Grand Green Osaka complex above Umeda station, opened recently. It has the Peacock Alley lounge every Waldorf has, and the park below is the largest new green space in the city. Nobody on FlyerTalk has stayed yet, the regulars there are wary of just-opened Hiltons, and people who had tried both told one member they preferred the Conrad. Treat it as unproven.

hotels.name: Patina Osaka
hotels.why: A luxury hotel one minute from Osaka Castle Park, with the lobby, the bar and an open rooftop on the 20th floor facing the castle. Rooms start at 50 square metres, the largest entry rooms in the city, and the top floor holds a listening room where a vinyl system plays a sunrise soundscape daily. Five restaurants and bars, a spa and an indoor pool. It opened in May 2025 and no FlyerTalk regular has stayed, so there is little traveller evidence yet.

hotels.name: Zentis Osaka
hotels.why: A boutique hotel in Dojimahama where the entry room is a 25-square-metre studio with a kitchenette counter, so a stay works like a small flat. The ground floor is an all-day cafe and bar that fills with locals rather than guests. Umeda and Nakanoshima are each about ten minutes on foot, and the Dojima blocks between them are offices, so eat towards the river.

hotels.name: Hotel Noum OSAKA
hotels.why: A design hotel at Tenmabashi facing the Okawa river, with a cafe and bar downstairs that stay open late. Kema Sakuranomiya park runs along the water outside, and its cherry trees are the ones Osaka turns out for in April. Osaka Castle is about fifteen minutes on foot. Rooms are small and simply fitted, so it suits a short stop rather than a base for a week.

hotels.name: NIKKO KANAYA HOTEL
hotels.area: Kami-Hatsuishi hillside, above the Daiya river
hotels.why: Japan's oldest surviving Western-style resort hotel, and the building is the reason to stay: carved woodwork through the halls and a main dining room from the old wings. The kitchen still cooks the French menu handed down through generations of Kanaya chefs. Toshogu shrine is fifteen minutes uphill on foot. Rooms in the old wings are creaky and plain next to the public rooms.

hotels.name: The Ritz-Carlton, Nikko
hotels.area: Oku-Nikkō, on the Lake Chuzenji shore
hotels.why: A lakeside resort on Lake Chuzenji with Mount Nantai across the water, and the first Ritz-Carlton anywhere built on a hot spring, piped down from the Yumoto source. FlyerTalk families rate the spa, the onsen and the cold plunges; one called three days here the favourite stop of a two-week trip. Oku-Nikko is 40 minutes of hairpins above the shrines, so it is a base for the outdoors rather than for temple mornings.

hotels.name: Hyatt Centric Kanazawa
hotels.why: A mid-range Hyatt two minutes from the west exit of the shinkansen station, with newer hardware than the local competition and more than a hundred works by Kanazawa artists and craftspeople through the house. The FlyerTalk regular who knows Japan best calls it not your ordinary Centric. The station side is the dull side of town, so allow the 15-minute walk to Omicho market and the old quarters.

hotels.name: Sōki Kanazawa
hotels.why: A design hotel opposite Omicho market, so the fish market is across the street and breakfast can be a rice bowl at a stall. Wabi-sabi rooms in wood and plaster, and a hot-spring public bath in the house. The castle park and Kenrokuen are a short walk. Rooms are on the small side, and the market is loud from early morning.

hotels.name: The Hotel Sanraku
hotels.why: A small luxury hotel between the castle and Omicho market, opened recently, with large stone-and-wood bathrooms and a breakfast reviewers single out. Both the market and the old geisha quarters are within a ten-minute walk. It has no bar or restaurant beyond breakfast, so evenings happen in town.

hotels.name: Hotel Wood Takayama
hotels.why: A modern-timber hotel steps from the historic district, with rooms lined in local cedar and evening sake tastings in the lounge. The morning market is two minutes away, which is the argument for staying inside the old town. Guests single out the staff. The old town empties by six, so book dinner before you arrive.

hotels.name: Cup of Tea Ensemble
hotels.area: Hida Takayama Onsen, walk to old town
hotels.why: A small hotel by Hida Takayama Onsen finished in thinned local timber and persimmon-tannin dye, so the town's woodwork is in the room itself. There is a cafe downstairs and little else; service is light. The old town is a walk away rather than at the door. It suits people who came for the craft.

hotels.name: IORI Stay (whole machiya)
hotels.why: A restored hundred-year-old machiya let whole to one party a night, with cypress baths in some houses and no lobby, no neighbours and no front desk. The shops and the morning market are at the door. Check-in is by arrangement and there is no service once you are in, so it suits a night you want to yourselves.

hotels.name: The Westin Sendai
hotels.area: Sendai Trust Tower, ~9-min walk from the station
hotels.why: The city's luxury pick by default, on the top floors of Sendai's tallest tower: rooms from the 28th floor look to the Pacific and the Zao range. A spa on the top floor, service guests praise, and nine minutes' walk to the station. FlyerTalk's regular finds the hotel itself drab, so book high and for the view rather than the public rooms.

hotels.name: Hotel Metropolitan Sendai East
hotels.why: A mid-range JR hotel built over Sendai station, so the shinkansen and the Matsushima trains are downstairs and a short stop costs no transit time. It is the newer of the two Metropolitan towers, the in-house dining is strong, and the arcades start across the concourse. The station side is not where the evening is, but the gyutan grills are a ten-minute walk.

hotels.name: Mitsui Garden Hotel Sendai
hotels.why: A business hotel off Jozenji-dori, the zelkova avenue, with an 18th-floor bath house that has an open-air pool looking over the city. It reopened in 2025 after a full renovation, and the interiors take their light from the trees on the avenue. Sendai station is about ten minutes' walk. Rooms are business-hotel sized, so the bath floor is where the stay happens.

hotels.name: KIRO Hiroshima by THE SHARE HOTELS
hotels.why: A design hotel in a converted downtown hospital, where the old indoor pool is now the lounge, with a coffee counter beside it and Seto-region art and furniture through the rooms. Rooms are simple and small, and the money that buys them is the money that buys okonomiyaki and Miyajima. The Peace Park is a fifteen-minute walk.

hotels.name: THE KNOT HIROSHIMA
hotels.why: A mid-range design hotel directly opposite the Peace Memorial Park, which makes it the best-placed bed in town for the memorial morning. Recently renovated, with work by Hiroshima artists in the lobby, a bistro downstairs and a rooftop bar over the river delta. The park side is quiet at night, so dinner is a ten-minute walk east.

hotels.name: RIHGA Royal Hotel Hiroshima
hotels.area: Motomachi, by the castle (5–10 min walk to Peace Park)
hotels.why: The city's grande dame, a tower by the castle in Motomachi, and the easy central choice for a one-night stop. Eight restaurants and bars, with the dining room on the 33rd floor looking over the delta towards the Inland Sea. The Peace Park is five to ten minutes' walk. The hardware is 1990s under the polish, so book high for the view.

hotels.name: The Ritz-Carlton, Fukuoka
hotels.why: The luxury answer in Fukuoka, on the top floors of a Tenjin complex, and this or nothing here according to FlyerTalk's Japan regulars. Rooms start at 50 square metres, the bar and pool on the 24th floor look over Hakata Bay, and the club lounge is rated among the best in Asia. One dissenter found it generic and detached from the city.

hotels.name: Miyako Hotel Hakata
hotels.why: A comfortable mid-range hotel over Hakata station whose rooftop spa has indoor and open-air hot-spring pools, which a city hotel rarely offers. Rooms are quiet and generous for their class, and the shinkansen and the airport subway are downstairs. Hakata is the transit side of town, so the Tenjin bars are a subway stop or a ten-minute taxi.

hotels.name: Hotel Il Palazzo
hotels.why: Japan's first designer hotel, and the red travertine facade and colonnade on the Naka river in Haruyoshi are the original ones. Sixty-two rooms, so it stays calm in a city of business towers. Nakasu's yatai stalls and Tenjin are each a short walk. The interiors were refreshed rather than rebuilt, so the rooms read of their period.

hotels.name: GALLERIA MIDOBARU
hotels.why: A design hotel on the steaming Mido-baru hillside where every room has its own hot-spring bath and a balcony over Beppu Bay. Contemporary art hangs through the halls and the restaurant cooks from a stone oven. It is the boutique alternative in a town of big old bathhouses. The hillside is a drive from the hells and the town, and the hotel runs a shuttle.

hotels.name: ANA InterContinental Beppu Resort
hotels.why: A polished onsen resort in the Horita highlands above the city: hot-spring baths, an infinity pool over the bay, and terrace suites with their own outdoor tubs. It is the one chain house here that works as a plush night rather than a business stop. The hells and the town are a short drive down the hill, by taxi or the hotel shuttle.

hotels.name: Suginoi Hotel
hotels.why: The Tanayu is the reason to come: five open-air pools terraced down the Kankaiji hillside, all of them facing Beppu Bay. An indoor water park sits alongside them. About 600 rooms across three wings, so the baths and the buffet draw a crowd; go to the Tanayu early or late. A shuttle runs down to the station and the hells.

hotels.name: THE BLOSSOM KUMAMOTO
hotels.area: Atop JR Kumamoto Station (Amu Plaza, floors 9–12)
hotels.why: A mid-range hotel on top of Kumamoto station: the lift runs from the shinkansen to a 27-square-metre modern Japanese room, which makes it the frictionless night between ryokan legs. A garden-view public bath, and the best hotel breakfast in the city. The castle and the arcades are a tram hop rather than a walk, so plan the evening as an outing.

hotels.name: OMO5 Kumamoto by Hoshino Resorts
hotels.area: Downtown — 5-min walk to the castle, on the arcades
hotels.why: A design hotel downtown on the covered arcades, with a rooftop terrace facing the illuminated castle keep five minutes' walk away. Bars and restaurants are at the door. Rooms are compact and cleverly fitted, so book the Utsuwa or Entaku twin rather than the low-beamed loft, which is tight for two with luggage.

hotels.name: Onyado Nono Kumamoto
hotels.area: By Sakuramachi Bus Terminal, ~5 min to the arcades
hotels.why: A ryokan-style hotel by the Sakuramachi bus terminal: shoes off at the door, tatami throughout, and a top-floor hot-spring bath with an outdoor pool and a sauna. Breakfast runs to sixty Kumamoto dishes and there is free late-night ramen. Rooms are small and the walls are thin. Skip it if the city stop is meant to be a break from tatami.

hotels.name: Hotel Indigo Nagasaki Glover Street
hotels.why: A restored 19th-century redbrick on Glover Street itself, inside the old foreign-settlement district, and the pick for a first visit. Breakfast is served in a former chapel, and reviewers keep naming the kakuni omelette, made with Nagasaki's braised pork belly. Oura Cathedral is next door. The slope up to the door is steep, so take a taxi with luggage.

hotels.name: Nagasaki Marriott Hotel
hotels.why: A chain hotel built over Nagasaki station, opened recently, where guests name the staff as the best part of the stay. Harbour and Mount Inasa rooms, a bayfront lobby, and the airport bus at the door, which makes it the natural base for flying out. The old town and Glover Garden are a tram ride south rather than a walk.

hotels.name: Garden Terrace Nagasaki
hotels.area: Akasako hillside, ~10 min from centre by taxi
hotels.why: A design resort on the Akasako hillside that frames the city's night panorama from the room and from the bath, which is the reason people book it. Folded timber and glass outside, though reviewers split on whether the interiors match it. Town is about ten minutes by taxi and there is nothing to walk to, so plan the evening around the view.

hotels.name: Setre Glover's House
hotels.why: A small hotel in the Minami-Yamate harbour quarter whose kitchen cooks creatively from Nagasaki produce, and dinner in the house is the reason to stay. Glover Garden, Oura Cathedral and Dejima are all on foot. A few rooms read dated, so ask for a renovated one when you book.

hotels.name: Sheraton Kagoshima
hotels.why: A full-service chain hotel by the Tenmonkan arcades, opened recently, with floor-to-ceiling Sakurajima views and a hot-spring floor drawing real onsen water. The eating district is at the door, which is what separates it from the hilltop hotels. Ask for a bay-facing room; the inland side looks at the city.

hotels.name: Shiroyama Hotel
hotels.why: The hilltop hotel above town, where the open-air onsen faces Sakurajima across the bay. A nationally ranked breakfast, and a Japanese-French dining room a FlyerTalk regular called spectacular. It is not walkable to anything, so use the free shuttle down to Tenmonkan and the station, which runs through the evening.

hotels.name: Good Fellows Resort U/Q
hotels.area: Iso Beach, by Sengan-en (~10 min from centre)
hotels.why: A two-room villa on Iso Beach next to Sengan-en, where Sakurajima fills the window and one room has a private ocean-view sauna. A roastery cafe sits below. Meals are house-only, last check-in is 17:30 and there is nothing to walk to, so treat it as a quiet night in rather than a base. It is too new to have reviews.
